2240: The pilot said just a few more minutes, a phrase that has never once been measured in actual minutes.
2241: The long taxi gave you time to gather your things, lose them, find them, and gather them once more.
2242: The wheels touched, and the person beside you exhaled like they had personally been flying the whole time.
2243: The plane inched into its spot as a person outside waved it in with the seriousness of landing a spaceship.
2244: A child three rows back asked if we were there yet, and two hundred adults silently wondered the same thing.
2245: The moment the plane stopped, the man behind you found his bag, his coat, and no way at all to actually leave.
2246: You touched the ground, and your ears, hours behind on the news, finally popped to tell you about it.
2247: The taxi to the gate was the slowest part of the whole journey, and somehow the part you remember least.
2248: Docked at last, the little bridge reaching for the door, and two hundred people stood up to wait more efficiently.
2249: The jet bridge is the one hallway on earth that belongs to nobody and charges no rent. Enjoy it briefly.
2250: You stepped off the plane into a new country, and its very first gift was a slightly different smell of the air.
2251: Every sign here means something to everyone but you, which you'll fix slowly, one confused glance at a time.
2252: You stepped over the little gap between plane and bridge, briefly a proud citizen of a two-inch void.
2253: The jet bridge sloped gently upward, and you climbed it like a person arriving to sort something out. You are.
2254: First breath of new air, and your lungs weren't quite sure whether to trust it. They decided to. Onward.
2255: You walked off the plane into a hallway that was, technically, already the new place. Congratulations, you're here.
2256: A whole city waits just past these doors, going about its afternoon, entirely unbothered by your arrival.
2257: You stepped onto new ground and it held, as ground tends to, but it still felt like a small quiet act of faith.
2258: At the door, the crew wished you a good stay with the practiced warmth of people who will not remember you.
2259: You stepped out and the terminal offered you a choice of long corridors, all quietly confident they led somewhere.
2260: The jet bridge smelled like every jet bridge, but the air waiting at the far end was brand new. Follow that.
2261: You took your first step into a city that has managed just fine for centuries without ever once meeting you.
2262: You walked off the plane unsure of the hour, the day, or which meal you were emotionally prepared for.
2263: Your body arrived on time. A smaller, sleepier part of it is still out over the ocean, taking the slow way here.
2264: You reached the mouth of the jet bridge and a whole unfamiliar day was simply standing there, waiting patiently.
2265: A new place doesn't roll out a carpet. It just keeps being itself while you quietly step into the middle of it.
2266: You stepped off the plane and every stranger within a mile kept doing exactly what they were doing. Rude. Fine.
2267: The first breath of a new place goes straight to your head. Or maybe that's just standing up after so long.
2268: You walked out of the plane into a city's ordinary weekday, uninvited and entirely delighted about it.
2269: The jet bridge delivered you like a parcel, gently and without ceremony, to the very edge of somewhere new.
2270: You crossed the threshold of the plane door and became, officially, a person who was Here instead of There.
2271: You arrived among people who were all extremely busy being from here, a skill you did not yet possess.
2272: You stepped off the plane and the new air had firm opinions about your jacket. You'll adjust. Everyone does.
2273: The first person you passed looked entirely at home, which felt, briefly, like a kind of showing off.
2274: First footstep on new soil, and it felt exactly like the last place, which is oddly reassuring and strange at once.
2275: Signs pointed the way to arrivals, as if arriving were a place and not the confused feeling you'd already achieved.
2276: The plane exhaled you into the terminal, and just like that you belonged to a whole different set of streets.
2277: You reached the bottom of the jet bridge and stood in a place that, until quite recently, had been purely theoretical.
2278: Past the gate, a crowd waited with signs and flowers, none of which, on close inspection, were for you.
2279: You took a big first breath of the new place and got mostly the smell of the plane you'd just left. Give it a minute.
